features.name: AI production maturity
features.description: Hands-on experience shipping AI or LLM-backed systems in production, especially with attention to reliability, evaluation, hardening, or failure modes.

levels.descriptor: No AI or LLM experience is mentioned.
AI experience is mentioned vaguely, with no clear production use or reliability detail.
The letter describes shipping AI-backed features or workflows in production.
The letter shows shipped AI work plus concrete attention to trustworthiness, evaluation, guardrails, or failure modes.

features.name: Academic credential level
features.description: The level of formal technical education or degree attainment the letter presents as relevant preparation for the role.

levels.descriptor: Bachelor's degree, equivalent, or no advanced degree is presented.
Master's degree is presented.
Doctoral degree is presented.

features.name: Agentic systems design
features.description: Direct experience designing or owning agent-based systems with explicit autonomy boundaries, supervision, permissions, audits, or control infrastructure.

levels.descriptor: No agentic systems experience is mentioned.
References agents in passing without clear ownership or design detail.
Describes a concrete agentic pipeline or tooling example.
Shows end-to-end ownership of agentic architecture, including boundaries, supervision, permissions, logging, or auditability.

features.name: Algorithmic fluency
features.description: Practical command of data structures and algorithms as evidenced through concrete engineering problem solving or system improvements.

levels.descriptor: No algorithmic evidence is given.
Makes a generic claim about data structures or algorithms.
Gives a specific example of choosing a better structure or redesigning logic algorithmically.
Gives a strong example showing substantial performance, scalability, or tractability improvement from algorithmic skill.

features.name: Collaboration and learning posture
features.description: Whether the applicant presents themselves as collaborative with specialists and internal users, and open to learning rather than purely solo or already-finished expertise.

levels.descriptor: Does not mention collaboration with security partners.
Implies support for other engineers, but not specifically partnership with security specialists.
Explicitly states readiness to work with security engineers or build for their workflows.
Shows explicit partnership mindset plus concrete evidence of learning from, serving, or collaborating with security specialists.

features.name: Developer enablement mindset
features.description: Whether the letter frames security engineering as helping other engineers do the safe thing easily through defaults, tooling, and reduced friction.

levels.descriptor: No developer-centered security philosophy is visible.
Shows generic interest in improving security but not specifically in making life easier for developers.
Explicitly talks about secure-by-default workflows, reducing friction, or helping teams do the right thing.
Strongly frames security as developer enablement, emphasizing defaults, tools, or guardrails over policing, process, or documents.

features.name: Evidence specificity
features.description: How much the letter supports its claims with concrete technical examples, mechanisms, outcomes, measurements, or other observable evidence.

levels.descriptor: Mostly offers generic assertions or checklist-style requirement matching.
Provides some specifics, but major claims remain abstract or unsubstantiated.
Gives several concrete, role-relevant examples showing what was built or changed.
Repeatedly backs claims with precise mechanisms, context, and outcomes that make the applicant's contribution easy to picture.

features.name: Go depth
features.description: How strongly the letter establishes Go as a central and meaningful production language in the applicant's work.

levels.descriptor: Go is missing, unclear, or only incidental.
Go is mentioned as a language used, but not as a main vehicle for work.
Go is clearly presented as the primary or day-to-day language.
Go is central to multiple production systems or explicitly tied to backend or security-infrastructure ownership.

features.name: Maintainer mindset
features.description: Whether the letter emphasizes reliability, maintainability, correctness, operational humility, and long-term care for systems rather than just feature shipping.

levels.descriptor: Shows no explicit maintainability or reliability orientation.
Implies care for quality but not as a recurring theme.
Clearly values maintainable, dependable systems or draws on maintenance experience.
Makes long-term operability a central lens, emphasizing inheritance, quiet resilience, or higher standards for security-critical software.

features.name: Narrative coherence
features.description: How well the letter forms a connected, well-flowing case for candidacy rather than a disconnected list of claims.

levels.descriptor: Reads mainly as a list of qualifications with little story connecting them.
Includes some motivation or a loose arc, but the connection from past experience to this role is not especially strong.
Builds a clear through-line from prior experience to interest in this role.
Presents a distinctive, memorable narrative or professional thesis that makes the application feel intentional and well-shaped.

features.name: Narrative distinctiveness
features.description: Whether the letter has a memorable, individualized voice or framing rather than reading like a generic template.

levels.descriptor: The letter reads like an interchangeable template or a flat list of qualifications.
The letter is competent but generic, with limited individuality in framing or voice.
The letter has a distinctive opening, viewpoint, or sustained framing device.
The letter is memorable and cohesive, with a clear throughline linking the opening idea, past work, and motivation for this role.

features.name: Offensive security practice
features.description: Ongoing attacker-oriented practice outside routine development work, especially through capture-the-flag participation or similar adversarial exercises.

levels.descriptor: No offensive-practice evidence is mentioned.
Mentions casual or occasional participation with little detail.
Shows regular participation presented as deliberate skill maintenance.
Shows strong results or serious competitive commitment that signals sustained offensive practice.

features.name: Open-source stewardship
features.description: Responsibility for public or upstream code beyond the applicant's immediate team, from fixing dependencies to maintaining projects used by others.

levels.descriptor: No open-source activity is mentioned.
Mentions occasional patches or minor contributions.
Shows regular contributions or maintainership of a small project.
Maintains a project with outside users or community responsibilities such as reviews, releases, issue handling, or roadmap decisions.

features.name: Ownership seniority
features.description: The level of independent responsibility, initiative, and direct ownership the letter claims for the work described.

levels.descriptor: The letter reads mostly as passive, resume-like claims with little direct ownership.
The letter shows some first-person ownership, but mainly on isolated tasks or narrow pieces of work.
The letter uses clear builder language around multiple shipped systems, automations, or redesigns.
The letter repeatedly shows end-to-end ownership, architecture, delivery, and ongoing operational responsibility.

features.name: Personal project ambition
features.description: The technical ambition, rigor, and seriousness of self-directed projects or side work described outside formal job responsibilities.

levels.descriptor: No personal project is mentioned.
Mentions a small utility or simple side project with limited technical stretch.
Describes a substantial side project with nontrivial systems or reliability concerns.
Describes an ambitious systems project that tackles distributed systems, storage, recovery, consensus, or similarly hard engineering problems.

features.name: Platform leverage orientation
features.description: Motivation for foundational or platform work whose impact compounds across many teams, services, or products.

levels.descriptor: Does not mention foundational leverage or broader organizational impact.
Expresses a general desire for scale or impact but without a clear platform orientation.
Explicitly wants infrastructure or foundational work that benefits many teams.
Repeatedly frames motivation around downstream leverage, central-platform responsibility, or quiet improvements inherited across an organization.

features.name: Production software experience
features.description: How much directly relevant professional experience the letter shows building, operating, maintaining, and launching production software systems.

levels.descriptor: Only minimal relevant experience is conveyed, with short tenure, narrow scope, or ambiguous ownership.
Clear early-career production experience is shown, but the record is still limited in depth or breadth.
Solid production background is shown through several years of work with repeated launch and maintenance responsibility.
Extensive directly relevant background is shown through long tenure plus broad multi-service responsibility.

features.name: Python depth
features.description: How concretely and convincingly the letter shows Python as a serious production language for services, tooling, automation, or back-end work.

levels.descriptor: Python is absent or only minimally mentioned.
Python is mentioned for light scripting or general familiarity.
Python is used regularly for tooling, automation, analysis, or services.
Python is presented as production-grade and central, with evidence of robust service or tooling development.

features.name: Role-specific alignment
features.description: How clearly the letter shows understanding of this exact role or team and maps the applicant's motivation and background to its specific mission, responsibilities, or requirements.

levels.descriptor: The motivation is formulaic and could fit almost any software-engineering application.
The letter shows some interest in security or Google, but the rationale is still fairly generic.
The letter gives clear, role-relevant motivation tied to the team's mission, working model, or problem space.
The letter gives memorable, well-tailored motivation that shows the applicant has thought specifically about this team's security-automation challenge.

features.name: Security assessment practice
features.description: Hands-on experience performing security reviews such as threat modeling, code review, attack-surface analysis, or remediation validation.

levels.descriptor: No assessment experience is shown.
Shows only general security interest or vocabulary without direct assessment work.
Shows direct experience performing security reviews or assessments.
Shows direct assessment experience plus method detail, such as threat models, attacker mindset, attack-surface mapping, or remediation verification.

features.name: Security automation insight
features.description: How well the letter understands security work as a scaling problem to be solved through principled automation, tooling, workflow design, and leverage.

levels.descriptor: Does not clearly articulate security automation as a central problem of the role.
Mentions reducing manual toil or automating repetitive work in general terms.
Clearly frames the role as scaling response capacity, expert attention, or organization-wide security effort.
Shows nuanced systems thinking about automation, such as variant analysis, triage strategy, scarce-expert amplification, or vulnerability response as a design problem.

features.name: Security credential strength
features.description: The presence, rigor, and relevance of formal external security certifications or credentials cited in the letter.

levels.descriptor: No security certification is mentioned.
A foundational certification such as Security+ is cited.
A hands-on practical certification such as OSCP is cited.

features.name: Security engineering mindset
features.description: Whether the letter articulates or reflects a mature philosophy, worldview, or identity about what security engineering is for and how it should be practiced.

levels.descriptor: No real security viewpoint is articulated beyond general interest.
The letter states that security matters, but the philosophy is thin or generic.
The letter presents a clear viewpoint, such as proactive assistance, quiet resilience, or defaults over policy.
The letter offers a nuanced security philosophy that is clearly tied to the applicant's engineering choices and the role's mission.

features.name: Vulnerability workflow automation
features.description: Direct ownership of tooling that automates vulnerability intake, triage, classification, routing, deduplication, prioritization, or related security-response workflows.

levels.descriptor: No vulnerability handling automation is mentioned.
Security automation is mentioned, but the triage workflow itself remains vague.
The letter clearly shows experience automating vulnerability intake, routing, or triage.
The letter describes a high-resolution triage pipeline with elements like classification, deduplication, prioritization, ownership, or clear manual-work reduction.

features.name: Writing polish
features.description: The degree of proofreading, spelling, grammar, and sentence-level mechanical correctness in the letter.

levels.descriptor: Frequent errors repeatedly interrupt reading or seriously undermine credibility.
Noticeable proofreading problems distract the reader more than once.
Contains some typos, but the letter remains easy to follow.
Mostly clean, with at most a minor slip.
Polished and effectively error-free at a professional standard.

other.name: Other
other.description: Genuinely distinct dimensions that do not clearly share an underlying construct with any larger recurring criterion.

levels.descriptor: Only Go is mentioned, or language breadth is unclear.
Shows Go plus one or two additional languages.
Shows Go plus several additional languages.
Shows Go plus broad multi-language experience across many systems.
